rules.title: CCCL Patron Conduct Policy (2026)
rules.summary: Same system policy as Concord. It regulates library-purpose activity and disruptive conduct but does not expressly resolve peaceful recording.
rules.constitutional_test: LPF purpose/reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality; separate recording doctrine
rules.enforcement_hook: Removal/suspension under library policy; criminal enforcement requires separate statutory authority.
open_questions: How Walnut Creek staff interpret recording/information gathering.

rules.title: CCCL Suspension Policy (2026)
rules.summary: Creates escalating suspensions and generic trespass escalation. Exact statutory bridge and process remain separate.
rules.constitutional_test: Due process + validity of underlying rule + exact trespass elements
open_questions: How City-controlled rooms interact with County suspension authority.

rules.title: CCCL Meeting Room Rules
rules.summary: System meeting-room rules are relevant but Walnut Creek includes City-managed rooms, so controller-specific rules must be separated.
open_questions: Which CCCL rules remain incorporated into City-managed Oak View/Las Trampas use?

rules.title: Walnut Creek Oak View / Las Trampas Facility Rental Rules
rules.summary: City rental program controls room use through reservation/operational terms. Exact live terms and recording implications must be evaluated separately from the ordinary library interior.
open_questions: Obtain current complete rental contract/terms and any recording restrictions.

rules.title: Rules for Exhibits / Display / Distribution of Non-Library Materials
rules.summary: The County intentionally opens exhibit/display/distribution channels while imposing subject/content limits, including restrictions on religious-service material and party/candidate advocacy. Those rules require a channel-specific LPF reasonableness/viewpoint-neutrality analysis and can be stress-tested from the public text now.
open_questions: Whether each subject restriction is reasonable in light of the opened channel and viewpoint neutral.
Whether Walnut Creek has adopted branch-specific additions.

rules.title: California Government Code §7927.105 — Library Patron Records
rules.summary: Confidentiality rule for library-maintained records, not a visitor camera statute.
rules.constitutional_test: Privacy context only unless another rule directly regulates visitor conduct.

rules.title: California Penal Code §632 — Confidential Communications
rules.summary: Applies only where statutory confidentiality elements are met; not a blanket interior-audio ban.
open_questions: Which counter/private-room interactions satisfy the confidentiality test?

rules.title: California Trespass / Public-Agency Obstruction Statutes
rules.summary: California trespass and public-agency-obstruction doctrine is now researched at the statewide level. A particular removal remains element- and fact-specific; a library policy violation alone does not establish the criminal-law branch.
rules.constitutional_test: Exact elements + constitutional savings clause + validity of underlying exclusion
open_questions: Which controller—City or County—asserts exclusion authority in each room/area?

rules.title: CCCL Patron Conduct Policy — Panhandling / Soliciting Donations
applies_to: library property, including potentially exterior areas covered by the policy
rules.summary: The County policy prohibits panhandling and soliciting donations or contributions on library property. Walnut Creek's Registry includes exterior plaza/park/lot subareas with strong TPF classifications as well as a purpose-limited interior, so the policy cannot be given one building-wide constitutional answer.
rules.constitutional_test: TPF exterior: applicable solicitation/time-place-manner scrutiny; LPF interior: purpose/reasonableness + viewpoint neutrality
rules.enforcement_hook: Library removal/suspension policy; criminal enforcement requires independent statutory authority.
open_questions: Whether the rule is actually enforced on the civic plaza, Civic Park connection, or surface lot.
What justification supports any exterior application.

rules.title: Walnut Creek Municipal Code ch. 10-8 — Public-Land Sign Placement
rules.summary: The current code restricts signs erected without property-owner permission and prohibits temporary signs from being attached to public objects or erected on publicly owned/maintained land. On its face, this is a placement/erection/attachment regime; it should not be silently converted into a ban on a person lawfully hand-carrying an expressive sign.
rules.constitutional_test: Exact conduct first: erected/placed/attached sign versus hand-carried expression; then forum and applicable sign/time-place-manner doctrine
rules.enforcement_hook: Municipal sign-code enforcement for signs within the chapter's scope.
open_questions: Whether City staff distinguish hand-carried signs from signs placed or erected on public property.
Whether any library-specific signage or guidance broadens the published code.

cpra_targets.target: Current CCCL internal staff/security guidance, training, scripts, supervisor instructions, and sign templates addressing photography, recording, observation, information gathering, solicitation, or the 'library-purpose activity' clause, including Walnut Creek-specific material.
cpra_targets.why: This should be combined with the Concord Library request at the system level rather than duplicated by branch.

cpra_targets.target: Current City of Walnut Creek Oak View and Las Trampas rental agreements, incorporated use rules, staff enforcement guidance, and any photography/recording or expressive-use restrictions.
cpra_targets.why: The City controls important LPF room channels whose complete live terms remain a material gap.

cpra_targets.target: Current City/Library signage orders or templates for the Walnut Creek Library plaza, entrances, garage/circulation, and interior addressing signs, solicitation, recording, assembly, or removal.
cpra_targets.why: The municipal sign code is public, but facility-specific posted mandates and their authority remain unverified.
